role_place: Monk of the Peribleptos monastery, Constantinople; compiler of the Panoplia Dogmatica commissioned by Emperor Alexios I Komnenos.
why_relevant: Writes the longest systematic Byzantine refutation of Islam (Title 28 of the Panoplia Dogmatica, 'Against the Saracens') with direct quotations of Qur'anic claims.
fame: Well known in Byzantine studies and in the history of Byzantine anti-Islamic polemic; Title 28 was first printed in Greek and Latin by Sylburg (1595) as 'Saracenica sive Moamethica'. Cited in modern scholarship on Byzantine views of Islam (Wickert 1910 dissertation).
orthodox_status: Orthodox monk and theologian, commissioned by the emperor; not canonised as far as I know (UNVERIFIED for a formal canonisation or local veneration).

role_place: Byzantine court official and historian (Constantinople, Nicaea); author of the Thesaurus of the Orthodox Faith and of the History (Chronike Diegesis).
why_relevant: Book XX of the Thesaurus is a dedicated chapter-by-chapter treatment of Islam ('On the superstition of the Agarenes'), with the sharpest label in the set: Islam as 'forerunner of the Antichrist'.
fame: Known as a historian (the History) and as a theologian of the Thesaurus; the Thesaurus is much less read than the History. The Book XX chapter on Islam is cited in modern work on Byzantine views of Islam (not searched in this run; UNVERIFIED which later authors cite it).
orthodox_status: Orthodox layman (court official, historian) and theologian; not a saint.

name_es: Fórmula anónima de abjuración (anatemas contra Mahoma)
name_en: Anonymous abjuration formula (anathemas against Muhammad), ritual text
name_orig: Ἀναθεματισμὸς τῶν Σαρακηνῶν / Ordo quo observatur super iis qui a Saracenis ad nostram fidem accedunt
language: Greek (Latin printed beside it in Migne PG 140)
role_place: Liturgical or ritual formula for the reception of converts from Islam into the Orthodox Church; anonymous.
why_relevant: Shows the ritual side of Byzantine anti-Islamic polemic: the converts renounce Muhammad and 'the god of Muhammad' in explicit anathemas.
fame: Known to specialists through Sylburg 1595 and the Migne PG 140 printing; attributed to the 12th century in the scholarly literature (UNVERIFIED for the date and for the controversy of 1180 under Manuel I Komnenos, which I did not check in a source).
orthodox_status: Anonymous ritual text; not an author. Listed as a bonus item, labelled anonymous/ritual.
